newsitem.title: FRANCE: Morocco passed on wheat tender, traders say.
newsitem.headline: Morocco passed on wheat tender, traders say.

text.p: Morocco appears to have passed on its August 4 tender to buy 120,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat, European grain traders on Tuesday.
"It looks as though they have passed. We are still waiting for the official confirmation," one exporter said.
Morocco had tendered for a total of 120,000 tonnes of wheat to be shipped in August and September.
Traders said the country had been offered wheat at less than $155 per tonne, cost and freight.
U.S. exporters said overnight the tender may have been cancelled because of price.
"They just think (the price) will go lower," one said.
U.S. wheat futures prices eased on Monday and were indicated lower again on Tuesday.
But European traders highlighted the bullish tone in wheat recently, and expressed disappointment the tender had flopped.
Traders said French wheat had nonetheless been uncompetitive for August shipment, even at the European Union's previous daily export tax of 0.5 Ecus per tonne.
The EU on Tuesday raised that tax to three Ecus per tonne and rejected bids for licences at the previous lower level.
